title: install-local: an uninstalled package still reads read-only until a restart, because engine.manifests keeps its id
body:
domain:server#3 · os-bill · session_01Utp6CbPxYq1wQmUNWvMZkC

Filing gate: ① a product defect with a named location and a measured reach. Found by the #30106 dev (os-dev report 6647662239 on #30106, `out_of_scope_findings` item 1), measured on the pre-fix and the fixed build. ⛔ Not a claim. No grade: triage sets it.

Business reason: an administrator who uninstalls a package (for example a `.custom` pair an older runtime installed as code, which PR #30207 now tells them to uninstall) gets a 200 "withdrawn from the running kernel", then still cannot create or customize that package's pair on the same instance until the server restarts. Nothing tells them a restart is needed.

Reader who acts: `domain:server`, the install-local uninstall door and `isWritablePackage` (`packages/metadata-protocol` package-writability) reading `engine.manifests`.

Dedupe (open and closed): `engine.manifests uninstall` (1 hit: #30106), `ensure-customization writable false uninstall` (4 hits: #30106, #29560, #29672, #28407; none covers this). **New.**

## What happens (measured by the #30106 dev)

1. `DELETE /api/v1/marketplace/install-local/ID` answers 200, "withdrawn from the running kernel".
2. `POST /api/v1/packages/BASE/ensure-customization` then answers 201 `created: true`, **`writable: false`**.

## Reading

`isWritablePackage` (package-writability) reads `engine.manifests` first; the engine only ever sets an entry there and the uninstall path never deletes it, so the id stays "provided by code" until a restart. This is a reading, not confirmed by a fix.

## Expected

After an uninstall answers success, the id no longer reads as code-provided on the running instance, or the uninstall answer says a restart is needed.
